Q: libvosk library not found A:

You can check the .nuget installation folder for vosk package and you will see that only packages for Windows, Mac and Linux were installed:

If you want to use vosk on Android, I'm afraid things are not as easy as importing the Android native library and magically use it on .net.

The native Android library is written on java/kotlin. You need to translate java/kotlin to c# to be able to use it on your .net maui Android application.

The process is quite large. My recommendation is using Maui.NativeLibraryInterop template adding com.alphacephei:vosk-android:0.3.75@aar dependency. You can find a step-by-step tutorial here.

In case you need help with the native Android project, you can find a sample here.

I don't know your project requirements, but by your post description, (in case you don't want to work with native code yourself) you could work with .net maui community toolkit SpeechToText instead, which already offers cross-platform coverage.

Q: Why does the PyCharm type checker give a warning about operators in the ComponentData class when they are indexed? A:

To shed some light on the warning, given m.v1[s], what are m.v1 and m.v1[s] types from static type-checker (PyCharm, etc.) point of view?

  • m is pyomo.environ.Model
  • pyomo.environ.Model inherits pyomo.core.ScalarBlock
  • which inherits pyomo.core.base.BlockData
  • which defines __getattr__() with -> Union[Component, IndexedComponent, Any] return type
  • hence PyCharm thinks v1 is Component | IndexedComponent | Any
  • pyomo.core.IndexedComponent defines __getitem__ with -> ComponentData return type
  • hence PyCharm thinks m.v1[s] is ComponentData
  • pyomo.core.base.component.ComponentData doesn't define __mul__ so PyCharm got confused and reports m.v1 * m.v2

Please correct me if I made a mistake.

Perhaps PyCharm should give up and consider m.v1 as Any, this way there will be no warnings, though no code completion as well.

Another option is for the library to introduce comprehensive type annotations if possible (stubs?) for the public API, including __mul__.
